subject: EdenWorks integration: sandbox access, auth, routing & fallback design
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@edenworks.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@edenworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: EdenWorks integration: sandbox access, auth, routing & fallback design

Hi Aisha + Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your engineers into a working sandbox by end of next week.

Recap (30m discovery)
- Primary goal: enable semantic search + structured Q&A over product manuals + allow tool-calling for order creation.
- Data residency: EU-hosted inference for production (must not leave eu-west).
- Throughput/latency target: p95 generation <= 200ms for routing decisions, <= 350ms for full tool-calls.
- Current infra preference: start on hosted sandbox, evaluate Dedicated for production.

Immediate asks / action items
1) Sandbox access: we'll provision a sandbox that includes an embeddings endpoint, a reranker pipeline, and a small LLM variant for prototyping. I attached a short playbook (edn_sandbox_playbook.pdf) with what we'll enable.
2) SDK & auth: which SDK languages do your engineers use (Node/Python/Java)? We support API keys, OAuth2 client-credentials, and mTLS. For the sandbox I can provision API keys, but for EU production we recommend either OAuth2 client-creds or mTLS. Please confirm.
3) Routing & fallbacks: proposed baseline policy: prefer low-latency variant for short queries (latency threshold 150ms), fallback to a cost-optimized quantized variant when load spikes or latency exceeds threshold. See attached proposed-routing.yaml for a first draft.
4) Structured output/tool-calling: we'll expose a function calling schema and safe JSON output enforcement. Do you have an existing schema for the order creation tool? If not, we can co-design a simple schema for the sandbox.
5) Embeddings + rerank: we recommend generating 1536-d embeddings with our eu-west endpoint, then use a cheap approximate nearest neighbor index for first-pass, followed by a reranker LLM for top-10 reordering.

Proposed timeline
- Tue/Wed: sandbox provision & API keys
- Thu: 30m integration workshop (SDK + auth + example pipeline)
- Following week: enable reranker & run perf smoke tests

Next steps for you
- Confirm SDK languages and preferred auth method for production.
- Share a sample order schema (if available) or say if you want Redwood to draft one.
- Preferred time slot for the integration workshop (we propose Thu 10/15 or Fri 10/16, 09:00–12:00 CET).

Attachments: edn_sandbox_playbook.pdf, proposed-routing.yaml

Thanks — I'll loop Ben and Rishi in for routing and cost/quantization details.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: EdenWorks integration: sandbox access, auth, routing & fallback design

Thanks Monica — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- SDKs: backend teams use Python (FastAPI) and a small Node.js microservice. Please include example snippets for both.
- Auth: for production we will need OAuth2 client-credentials backed by our IdP (Azure AD). For the sandbox API keys are fine — we'll use them to validate integration.
- EU requirement: all production inference (embeddings + generation) must run in eu-west; sandbox can be hosted in EU as well if possible.
- Order schema: attaching the current (intermediate) order schema used by our order-service — it's not final but should be enough to draft a tool-calling schema.

A couple of asks: can you provide a rough cost delta between using the low-latency variant vs the cost-optimized quantized fallback (for a baseline of ~1M tokens/mo)? Also please confirm whether the reranker pipeline will introduce extra token charges for top-k re-runs.

Preferred workshop slots: Thu 2026-10-15 10:30–11:00 CET or Fri 2026-10-16 09:30–10:00 CET.

Thanks,
Aisha Kapoor
Head of Platform Engineering | EdenWorks

Subject: Re: EdenWorks integration: sandbox access, auth, routing & fallback design

Thanks Monica / Aisha — adding a few engineering details from the infra side so the Sandbox behaves like a realistic prod-slice: 

- Routing policy suggestion (high-level):
  * primary route: low-latency LLM (eu-west-small-llm) with latency-slo = 150ms p95
  * fallback 1: quantized variant (eu-west-quant-q4) with cost_weight = 0.45 when p95 breach or queue depth > 75%
  * fallback 2: cached-prefix quick-responses via KV cache for repeat queries (no token charges for cached responses)
  * critical: region pinning rule for all production requests from EdenWorks to eu-west

- Cost note: rough delta (very rough ballpark) vs. token consumption for 1M tokens/month:
  * low-latency variant: ~$1,200/mo
  * quantized fallback: ~$380/mo
  * reranker overhead: expect ~10–25% additional token usage depending on top-k (k=10 implies 10x ranking calls but can be optimized via candidate batching)

- SDK & auth: We'll prepare short Python and Node samples using OAuth2 client-credentials; for the sandbox I'll put together API-key examples and a step-by-step to exchange for a short-lived token.

- Structured output: Redwood will support function/tool calling with enforced response schema validation. For order creation we'll accept your order JSON and map fields into the tool call. If there's ambiguity on required fields, we'll make the tool call strict in prod and permissive in sandbox.

I'll draft a minimal route-policy YAML and share it to the folder. Monica — can you provision the sandbox with EU region preference? Rishi, can you eyeball the cost numbers and adjust if I'm off.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
